newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenians begin voting in electoral referendum.
newsitem.headline: Slovenians begin voting in electoral referendum.

text.p: Slovenians began voting on Sunday in a referendum on changes to the electoral system, one month after an inconclusive general election left neither right nor left with a mandate to run the government.
Some 1.5 million people were eligible to vote for one of three different electoral models.
Polls opened at 7 a.m. local time (0600 GMT) and were due to close at 1800 GMT, when the first unofficial results were expected.

Recent opinion polls have suggested a two-round majority system proposed by the centre-right Social Democrats was likely to get the most support. Under this model, a candidate who managed in the end to secure an absolute majority would succeed in each of Slovenia's 88 voting districts.

The centre-left Liberal Democrats (LDS), Slovenia's strongest party, favours a proportional representation system in which each party would put up a list of 88 candidates. At present each party is represented in each electoral district with one candidate.

The National Council, the lower house of Slovenia's parliament, proposes a model combining Social Democrat and LDS models, with half of the 88 candidates elected on the basis of a two-round run-off system and the other half by proportional representation.
Turnout at the parliamentary poll on November 10 was 73.7 percent.
The final official result will be announced on Thursday.
